yes_but.evidence: Existing surveys focus on subsets of mobile edge technologies.

contribution.evidence: Lists taxonomy across nodes, applications, and future directions.

organization.evidence: Presents section roadmap and organization figure/table references.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focus limited to mobile ECNs (aerial, ground, spatial, maritime) and their applications.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate mobile ECNs; note survey gap; lay background; classify nodes; compare; cover applications (single vs integrated); list future directions; conclude.

axes: Node type (aerial, ground vehicular, spatial, maritime)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro uses organization figure and glossary table; background includes architecture and acronym table; each node section uses figures for mobility/channel examples and ends with summary; comparison section has a table; application sections interleave scenario figures.

figures.purpose: show survey structure and node taxonomy

lesson_blocks.lesson: Reuse the mobility/channel/energy/examples+summary pattern to make each node class comparable.
Compress differences across node types before diving into applications.
Separate single-node applications from integrated-node applications to clarify design assumptions.
Tie future enablers (mmWave, RIS, FL, blockchain) back to mobility and integration challenges.

synthesis.aha_moment: A repeated subsection template across four node categories creates a digestible taxonomy that later feeds into application mapping and future directions.

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce node class or topic, then enumerate sub-dimensions (mobility, channel, energy) before examples and summaries.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Intro gap with node-class coverage claim
steps: State benefits and demand for mobile ECNs.
Note that prior surveys cover only subsets of node types.
List contributions spanning all four node classes and integrated architectures.
Show an organization figure to preview taxonomy and applications.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Anchors novelty on coverage breadth and orients the reader early.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Per-node-class template
steps: For each node class, cover mobility behavior, channel model, energy model, examples.
Repeat identically for all classes to aid comparison.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Consistency makes a multi-class taxonomy easier to digest and compare.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Mid-article comparison checkpoint
steps: After covering all classes, add a short comparison section (mobility, coverage, channel).
Use a table to compress contrasts.
Use this as a bridge into applications.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Re-syncs readers after lengthy taxonomy and prepares them for application mapping.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Applications split into single vs integrated nodes
steps: First present applications for each standalone node class.
Then present integrated-node applications by pairing types.
Highlight design assumptions unique to each grouping.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Separating single from integrated scenarios clarifies scope and avoids conflating assumptions.

notes: Counts are heuristic; many figures. Headings include span tags. No evaluation framework; focus on taxonomy and applications.
